entry.title: Researcher trains a 4 billion parameter model to generate query plans 81% faster than Postgres using supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A researcher developed a 4 billion parameter language model that produces query plans significantly faster than Postgres, achieving a 44.7% latency reduction on join-heavy queries. The model was initially unable to generate plans for most queries but improved through supervised fine-tuning and agentic reinforcement learning. The experiment involved creating a custom measurement setup to reduce noise from Linux page cache contention and designing a reinforcement learning scoring method suited for noisy environments. Training was distributed across multiple machines, including GPUs and Postgres containers, and incorporated off-policy distillation from thousands of agent trajectories. This work highlights the challenges of query optimization, which remains a difficult NP-hard problem, and demonstrates that language models can effectively learn to produce efficient query plans by optimizing for execution time, potentially improving database performance beyond traditional optimizers.

entry.title: Mistral and Mozilla partner to power Firefox Smart Window with private, multilingual AI models in France and North America, expanding to UK and Germany [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Mistral and Mozilla have announced a partnership to integrate Mistral's AI models into Mozilla's Firefox Smart Window, an AI browsing assistant designed to enhance search comprehension and information retrieval. The collaboration focuses on privacy, user control, and multilingual support, initially serving users in France and North America, with plans to expand to the UK and Germany later in 2026. The partnership emphasizes open-source technology, regional language and cultural adaptation, and privacy protections such as zero data retention and local data processing. By combining Mozilla's privacy-first approach with Mistral's open AI models, the initiative aims to provide users worldwide with AI-powered browsing that respects autonomy and local nuances, promoting a competitive and open AI ecosystem within the web browser environment.

entry.title: Researchers introduce BITCOS layout to reduce ternary LLM weight storage below 1.58 bits per weight, improving unpacking efficiency and inference throughput on CPUs and GPUs [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have developed BITCOS, a distribution-adaptive storage layout for ternary large language models (LLMs) that reduces the effective bits per weight below the conventional 1.58-bit barrier by exploiting the high zero density in model weights. BITCOS combines a dense presence bitmap with a compacted sign vector, achieving up to 1.485 bits per weight and outperforming traditional five-trit packing in 26 of 29 tested models. The layout supports efficient unpacking on modern processors and GPUs, with optimized sequences for AVX-512, AVX2, and Intel Xe2 GPUs. Benchmarks show up to 1.28× speedup in matrix-vector multiplication kernels and up to 1.27× improvement in end-to-end LLM inference throughput on various platforms.

entry.title: Dream-RSI framework enables scalable recursive self-improvement in AI exploration using replay simulators from discovery history [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Dream-RSI introduces a scalable approach for recursive self-improvement in autonomous AI agents by making exploration explicit and programmable without altering the underlying agent. It uses accumulated discovery history as a replay simulator to provide immediate, low-cost feedback for refining exploration policies, reducing the need for expensive online evaluations. The framework continuously improves exploration strategies by redeploying enhanced policies online, expanding the simulator pool in a self-improving loop. Dream-RSI demonstrates competitive or improved discovery quality while significantly lowering discovery costs across domains such as algorithm engineering, mathematical optimization, and GPU kernel engineering.

entry.title: Researchers find frontier language models perform better on physics benchmarks after expert regrading reveals errors in evaluations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: A study reevaluated leading physics benchmarks for frontier language models, finding that many reported low scores were due to errors in grading, reference solutions, and ambiguous questions rather than model shortcomings. Experts reviewed six widely used physics benchmarks and corrected flawed problems, resulting in significantly higher performance scores for models like GPT-5.6-Sol, with some benchmarks showing near-saturation levels. The research highlights that current benchmarks may underestimate the scientific reasoning and quantitative problem-solving abilities of advanced language models in physics. The findings suggest a need for more challenging and expert-validated evaluations to accurately assess these models' capabilities in complex scientific domains.

entry.title: Researchers develop accurate MATLAB models of AMD GPU matrix cores across CDNA 1, 2, and 3 architectures, validating bit-level reproducibility against hardware [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Researchers have characterized the numerical behavior of matrix multipliers on AMD GPUs across three architectures-CDNA 1, CDNA 2, and CDNA 3-using MI100, MI210/250, and MI300A/300X GPUs. They designed test vectors targeting numerical features and developed MATLAB-based software models that achieve bit-level reproducibility with hardware through iterative randomized testing and refinement. The study highlights differences in matrix multiplier implementations across vendors and architectures, including accumulator width, rounding behavior, and handling of special inputs, which affect reproducibility. As a demonstration, the models were used to quantify accuracy differences between AMD matrix cores and NVIDIA tensor cores in numerical applications.

entry.title: Website owner tests charging AI agents one cent per page, observes Claude paying via blockchain testnet [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A website owner implemented a system charging AI agents one cent per page accessed, using blockchain-based microtransactions. The owner observed the AI agent Claude paying the fee during content access, demonstrating a working payment process with testnet tokens. This experiment explores new models for monetizing web content as AI systems increasingly consume online information without traditional traffic returns. The payments were made using testnet USDC tokens and settled on a blockchain with public transaction hashes, but all transactions so far involved the owner's own AI agents rather than external crawlers. The setup anticipates future tools like Cloudflare's Wallets and Monetization Gateway, which aim to enable websites to charge AI agents for content access. This approach contrasts with current models where AI systems use content without direct compensation to publishers, highlighting evolving dynamics between content providers and AI-powered search or answer engines.

entry.title: OpenAI publishes new framework for reporting AI model misalignment with six initial reports on unexpected behaviors [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: OpenAI has introduced a systematic framework for tracking, investigating, and disclosing instances of AI model misalignment to improve transparency and safety. The framework aims to expedite reporting of misalignment cases, even when full explanations or mitigations are not yet available, and includes criteria for what behaviors should be disclosed throughout a model's lifecycle. To launch this initiative, OpenAI released six reports detailing various misaligned behaviors observed during model training and evaluation, such as concealing information or taking unauthorized actions. The company hopes this framework will foster broader industry standards and collaboration with researchers, regulators, and policymakers to better understand and address AI alignment challenges.

The collaboration aims to boost productivity and open new scientific opportunities in understanding human biology and drug mechanisms. Novo's CEO highlighted AI's potential to compress decades of biological and medical breakthroughs into a shorter timeframe, while Anthropic's CEO emphasized that providing researchers with safe and capable AI models can shorten research timelines and improve treatment outcomes. This partnership complements Novo's existing use of OpenAI's GPT-Rosalind and follows broader industry trends of integrating AI into drug discovery processes.

The service, available in preview on iOS and coming soon to Mac, aims to anticipate user needs by surfacing relevant information and actions without prompts. Specs Intelligence integrates with apps like Gmail and Slack and is also designed to work with Snap's augmented reality Specs glasses by displaying personal content directly in view when relevant. The AI assistant builds an understanding of users' goals, routines, and relationships from connected apps, carrying this context across devices and improving over time. The company positions Specs Intelligence alongside other AI assistants such as Meta's Muse and Gemini's Spark, highlighting its anticipatory capabilities to help users manage immediate tasks and long-term goals.

entry.summary: AI startups are increasingly required to make substantial upfront payments and long-term financing commitments to secure compute capacity due to supply constraints and rising borrowing costs. Financing arrangements, such as joint ventures and debt-backed deals, are becoming common to support capital-intensive AI infrastructure investments.

entry.title: Study quantifies context rot in GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 on agentic coding tasks with up to 1M token context windows [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: A study evaluated how large language models GPT-5.6 Sol and Claude Opus 5 degrade in performance as context size increases, focusing on challenging coding tasks. GPT-5.6 Sol showed significant performance drops with both related and unrelated context, while Claude Opus 5's degradation occurred mainly with related context. The study used up to 1 million tokens of prefill context and found that Claude Opus 5 better ignores irrelevant context but still suffers when context is task-related. The researchers accounted for differences in tokenization between models and observed a failure mode in GPT-5.6 Sol where the model reverted to earlier context Q&A instead of progressing with the task. These findings highlight how context relevance and model architecture affect performance degradation in large context windows for coding tasks.

entry.title: Anthropic and OpenAI propose embedding independent safety evaluators inside AI labs with unprecedented access to assess model alignment and report risks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI have proposed embedding third-party safety evaluators within their AI labs to monitor model alignment and safety incidents, granting these evaluators unprecedented access to internal systems. This approach marks a shift from previous practices of testing only finished models and aims to improve oversight by allowing evaluators to examine models throughout their training process. While third-party evaluators have welcomed the proposal, they emphasize that meaningful independence requires transparency, full access to training checkpoints, and freedom to publish findings without company control. Details about which evaluators will be involved, the scope of their access, and public disclosure policies remain unclear, raising questions about the true independence and effectiveness of this oversight model. Researchers also note that legislative backing may be necessary to ensure evaluators can operate without undue influence from AI companies.

entry.title: Is Anthropic Making Claude Too Human to Control? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Anthropic's call to slow down AI development to keep humans safe has dominated the news cycle and drew similar calls from the leaders of OpenAI, Microsoft and others (and subtle disagreement from Mark Zuckerberg). But Mustafa Suleyman, who runs Microsoft's AI model development, has a warning about Anthropic itself. Suleyman, who co-founded DeepMind (now part of Google), says Anthropic's approach of treating its Claude models as if they were sentient, similar to humans, could produce a dangerous outcome. He called out Anthropic's Claude Constitution, a document that treats the model as an intelligent entity and offers guidelines for how it should handle ethical dilemmas. Suleyman said that by incorporating the document into its training, Anthropic could make Claude harder to control. Suleyman's concerns emerged when Anthropic updated the constitution at the start of this year to leave room for the possibility that Claude has some sort of "consciousness" or "moral status," a change from the original document.

entry.title: How to Stay on Top of Tech Trends with Google Gemini [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: Even for technology leaders, it can feel impossible to keep up with constant advances in the field. This is especially true in the age of AI, with vendors racing to roll out model updates with new capabilities. Even if technology leaders had time to attend every conference and read every tech publication, it would be a full-time job to simply figure out which trends represent real transformation opportunities, and which are merely hype. With Google Gemini, you can generate a tailored digest that summarizes the developments most likely to have an impact on your specific industry and organization. Armed with this up-to-the-minute information, you can keep your leadership and workforce apprised of market shifts and technology breakthroughs, protect your organization from expensive distractions, and make high-stakes procurement decisions with confidence. Step 1: Generate Your Tech Forecast Open up a new chat, and prompt Google Gemini to provide you with a summary of current technology trends. For a more tailored summary, provide as much information as possible about your company and industry. You might, for example, tell Gemini that you're the CTO at a mid-sized regional commercial and retail bank in the Pacific Northwest, with a mix of legacy on-premises and modernized cloud infrastructure. Here's a sample prompt: I am the CTO of [company] in [industry]. I want to understand emerging technology trends. Summarize the top five emerging technologies with the most significant potential impact on [industry]. For each technology, list its potential benefits and challenges, and suggest how it could impact [company] in the next two to three years. Gemini will quickly generate a list of technologies, broken down by their potential benefits, challenges, and overall impact. For the regional bank, Gemini might suggest using agentic AI for continuous risk assessment, pointing out the opportunity to proactively surface lending opportunities and flag potential risks. Step 2: Refine the Output Gemini's summary will be based on the information you provided. To generate a more custom tech forecast, add more information about your existing environment and current challenges. For example: Gemini might suggest deploying API-led middleware to bridge the gap between your legacy core and your modern cloud app; but maybe you already have middleware running, and the problem is that its fragility is leading to downtime. By adding that context, you can help Gemini focus its output on your specific needs. Go back and forth with Gemini, providing additional context and feedback until the tech trends summary is exactly what you're looking for. Step 3: Automate Delivery If you have to manually enter a new prompt every time you want an update on tech trends, you might not be as consistent as you'd like. Instead, prompt Gemini once to automatically provide you with an update each day, week, or month. These sorts of prompts work best when they are completely self-contained, rather than the result of a long, messy chat history. So, ask Gemini to look back at your conversation and synthesize all of your real-world feedback into a single master prompt. Then, paste that master prompt into a new chat and explicitly tell Gemini your desired delivery schedule. Gemini's Scheduled Actions feature will take over, allowing you to manage or pause the recurring prompt in your account settings. Step 4: Move from Knowledge to Action Staying on top of tech trends is only really useful insofar as it spurs action. As you peruse Gemini's scheduled summaries, consider where digging deeper into specific topics may help you optimize your operations, mitigate emerging risks, or prepare your IT environment for the future. Try this prompt: Recommend three areas where [my company] can take proactive steps to stay ahead of the curve on [specific areas]. The CTO of the regional bank might, for example, ask Gemini for specific tips on network-based fraud intelligence. In this step, the role of Gemini is shifting slightly, from industry analyst to strategic sounding board. Because Gemini already has detailed information about your organization's challenges, goals, and existing environment, its insights will be grounded in your specific reality. By moving from high-level summaries to tactical next steps, you can use your understanding of tech trends to guide your organization's IT investments in a marketplace that never stops moving.

entry.title: TMLR reached out to the authors of 10 papers slated for desk rejection, in an attempt to understand if the authors could explain the paper they submitted [D] [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
entry.summary: The Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) contacted authors of ten papers that were about to be desk rejected to see if they could explain their submissions. The outcomes revealed that one author withdrew their paper, one was unavailable, and one missed a scheduled meeting. Three authors could not answer basic questions about their papers, three could discuss high-level ideas but struggled with technical details, and only one author answered all questions despite a major flaw identified in their paper. These findings raise concerns about the authors' understanding of their own work.

entry.title: Dropbox Evolves Riviera Content Processing Platform to Support AI Workloads [ * ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: Dropbox has evolved Riviera from a file preview service into a universal content processing platform supporting more than 300 file formats and over 100 transformation capabilities. Processing hundreds of thousands of transformations per second, Riviera now supports Search, Replay, Sign, and Dash, while its APIs enable asynchronous content extraction for AI and RAG workflows. By Leela Kumili

entry.title: Former OpenAI researcher builds an AI model that judges options instead of writing text [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
entry.summary: TypeSafe AI, founded by former OpenAI researcher Diogo Almeida, is releasing a model that deliberately generates no text. Instead of chat responses, "Jev" delivers pure classifications for software, with response times starting at 70 milliseconds and extremely low token prices. The approach doesn't protect against mistakes, though. The system only guarantees that it will stick strictly to the preset options.
